title: Noun に 来ます
shortExplanation: Used to express coming to a place.
longExplanation: The grammar point Noun に 来ます is used to indicate that someone or something comes to a specific place. The noun before に indicates the destination or place, while the verb 来ます expresses the action of coming. (Similarly, 'Noun に 行きます' means 'go to [Noun],' and 'Noun に 帰ります' means 'return to [Noun].')

examples.jp: 友達が私の家に来ます。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga watashi no ie ni kimasu.
examples.en: My friend will come to my house.

examples.jp: 今晩、父が駅に迎えに来ます。
examples.romaji: Konban, chichi ga eki ni mukae ni kimasu.
examples.en: Tonight, my father will come to pick me up at the station.

examples.jp: 明日、先生が学校に来ます。
examples.romaji: Ashita, sensei ga gakkou ni kimasu.
examples.en: Tomorrow, the teacher will come to school.

examples.jp: 有名な歌手がこの街に来ます。
examples.romaji: Yuumei na kashu ga kono machi ni kimasu.
examples.en: A famous singer will come to this town.
